title: Shamir secret sharing
description: Shamir's scheme splits a secret into n shares where any t reconstruct it but t-1 reveal nothing — a polynomial of degree t-1 through the secret, one point per party. It's the foundation of MPC: data stays split across parties, and computation happens on shares, never on reconstructed secrets.
method: Pick random polynomial f with f(0)=secret; share i gets f(i); any t points interpolate f(0); fewer give no information.
usage: Choose t for your adversary model; distribute shares over trust boundaries; never assemble shares in one place.

demo.code:
secret, shares = 42, [(1, 61), (2, 80), (3, 99)]  # f(x)=42+19x
x1,y1,x2,y2 = shares[0][0],shares[0][1],shares[1][0],shares[1][1]
rec = (y1*x2 - y2*x1)//(x2-x1)
print('reconstructed from 2 shares:', rec)

title: BGW protocol
description: Ben-Or, Goldwasser, Wigderson brought MPC to arithmetic circuits with Shamir shares: additions are local, multiplications need one interaction round (degree reduction). BGW tolerates t < n/3 malicious parties — information-theoretic security, no crypto assumptions at all.
method: Shamir-share inputs; add locally; multiply with degree-reduction interaction; reconstruct the output.
usage: Use for arithmetic MPC (statistics, ML) with honest-majority assumptions.

demo.code:
print('shares of a, b; c = a*b via degree reduction (1 round)')
print('output reconstructed; no party saw a or b')

title: Threshold cryptography
description: Threshold signatures and decryption split a key across n parties; any t can sign/decrypt, fewer cannot. It's MPC for a single operation — protecting CA keys, crypto wallets, and root credentials so no single party (or thief) holds the key.
method: Distributed key generation; t parties collaborate per operation; the full key never exists in one place.
usage: Protect high-value keys with threshold schemes; choose t for your availability/security tradeoff.

demo.code:
print('3-of-5 threshold signature: parties 1,3,4 collaborate')
print('valid signature produced; full key never existed anywhere')

title: Private set intersection
description: PSI lets two parties learn the intersection of their sets without revealing the rest — the protocol behind private contact discovery (Signal) and ad measurement. Modern PSI runs on millions of items with Diffie-Hellman or OT-based constructions.
method: Hash items into bins; run DH or OT-based intersection per bin; reveal only matching items.
usage: Use for private matching; pad sets to hide sizes if size itself is sensitive.

demo.code:
a, b = {'alice','bob','carol'}, {'bob','dave'}
print('PSI result: intersection computed, neither side reveals non-matching items')

title: MP-SPDZ framework
description: MP-SPDZ implements 30+ MPC protocols behind one Python-like frontend: write the computation once, run it under semi-honest, malicious, honest/dishonest majority protocols. It's the compiler that made MPC experimentally accessible — protocol choice becomes a flag, not a rewrite.
method: Write in the MP-SPDZ DSL; compile; select the protocol backend; run across parties.
usage: Prototype in MP-SPDZ; benchmark protocol backends for your function; deploy the winner.

demo.code:
print('program: sfix average of private inputs')
print('run: -b semi-honest (fast) vs -b malicious (safe) — same program')

title: MPC for private ML inference
description: Two or three servers jointly evaluate a neural network on a client's private input: the client secret-shares its data, servers compute under MPC, and only the client learns the result. Private inference without trusting any single server — deployed for medical and financial models.
method: Secret-share the input; evaluate the network layer by layer under MPC; return shares of the output to the client.
usage: Use for high-value private inference; quantize models to reduce MPC cost.

demo.code:
print('client shares x-ray; 3 servers evaluate tumor-model under MPC')
print('client reconstructs: diagnosis; servers learned nothing')

title: Oblivious transfer
description: Oblivious transfer is MPC's core primitive: the sender has two messages, the receiver picks one, the sender doesn't learn which, the receiver learns nothing about the other. OT extension (IKNP) amortizes base OTs into millions cheaply — nearly all practical MPC runs on OT extension.
method: Base OTs via public-key crypto; extend to millions with symmetric crypto (IKNP); build garbled circuits and GMW on top.
usage: Use OT extension libraries; never implement base OT yourself.

demo.code:
print('sender: [m0, m1]; receiver choice: 1')
print('receiver learns m1 only; sender learns nothing about the choice')

title: SPDZ (malicious majority)
description: SPDZ handles the hard case: malicious parties in dishonest majority, using somewhat-homomorphic encryption for a preprocessing phase that generates authenticated multiplication triples. Online phase is fast information-theoretic MPC with MACs catching cheaters — abort on misbehavior.
method: Preprocess: generate Beaver triples with MACs; online: consume triples for multiplications; verify MACs; abort on failure.
usage: Use when parties don't trust each other; the offline phase can run before inputs are known.

demo.code:
print('offline: 1M triples generated (SHE)')
print('online: multiplication = 2 opens + MAC check -> cheater caught, abort')
